Hi Samir / Priya 

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our demo + the model shortlist we recommend for your conversational analytics / summarization use case (attached). High-level guidance below: 

1) Recommendation summary (shortlist)  see attached acme_model_shortlist.xlsx for numbers:
   - redwood-rlm-13b-q2 (quantized): Best balance of cost and latency for medium-length summaries (avg token length ~250). Good throughput with Redwood Dedicated + autoscaling.
   - openplex-7b-ft: Lowest inference cost; strong on short replies and extraction tasks but needs careful prompt engineering for long-form summaries.
   - instruct-70b (fp16): Highest quality on edge cases / domain-specific terminology but 2-3x cost and higher latency. Consider as fallback for critical queries.

2) Tradeoffs (cost / latency / quality)  short rationale in the sheet:
   - redwood-rlm-13b-q2: ~35-45ms/token on A100-ish infra (typical config), cheaper per-token than instruct-70b by ~60% with small hit in rare-case accuracy.
   - openplex-7b-ft: <25ms/token and lowest cost, but has more hallucination on abstractive tasks without extra eval/prompt sets.
   - instruct-70b: ~90-120ms/token, best for complex legal/financial language.

3) Suggested evals / next steps:
   - Run a 1-week pilot where you run ~2k real-user prompts through redwood-rlm-13b-q2 and openplex-7b-ft in A/B to measure latency/cost/quality.
   - Use the attached prompt set (acme_prompt_set_v1.txt) and our MAP-eval-template.md to capture precision/regression metrics.
   - Dev (cc) will share benchmark links and recommended batching/quantization configs for your infra.

4) Ask: Can you confirm the pilot scope (number of prompts / date range) and whether you want us to provision a Dedicated pool for the pilot? I can draft an MOP and a HubSpot milestone once you confirm.

Attachments: acme_model_shortlist.xlsx, acme_benchmarks.pdf, acme_prompt_set_v1.txt

Thanks  happy to jump back on a quick call if useful.

Hi Samir / Priya 

Thanks for the questions  wanted to address them with concrete numbers and proposed guardrails. TL;DR: token-level numbers + infra overhead map to ~180-400ms E2E depending on model & payload; we recommend a short A/B pilot with automated regression checks using prompt buckets. Details below.

End-to-end latency guidance (typical):
- openplex-7b-ft (q4_0 quantized on T4): ~18-28ms/token inference + ~60-80ms network + client-side processing => expected median E2E ~180-300ms for 150-token outputs.
- redwood-rlm-13b-q2 (A100 / fp16 run with KV cache warm): ~35-45ms/token + ~60-80ms overhead => median ~230-400ms E2E depending on batching and cold vs warm cache.
- instruct-70b (fp16 on A100x): ~90-120ms/token => E2E typically >600ms for longer outputs; not ideal for the 300ms target.

Cost estimate (ballpark, hosted pricing model):
- openplex-7b-ft: ~$0.70 per 1k tokens processed; for 100k summaries at avg 200 input+output tokens => ~20M tokens => ~$14k/month.
- redwood-rlm-13b-q2: ~$1.80 per 1k tokens => ~20M tokens => ~$36k/month.
- instruct-70b: ~$5.00 per 1k tokens => ~100k summaries at larger token counts (~400 tokens) => ~$200k/month.

Recommended guardrails for regression detection:
1) Prompt bucketing: Split your prompt set into 8 buckets (by template / intent). Run weekly MAP evals per bucket.
2) Thresholds: Fail if mean factuality drops >3 points or if latent hallucination rate >5% for critical buckets.
3) Canary rollout: Start pilot with 10% traffic to new variant, run automated scoring on the prompt set (we can host the eval harness), and promote if pass.
4) Monitoring: Enable token-level cost and latency tracing + per-route error alerts in Redwood Console.

Benchmarks and links:
- Lightweight bench: https://bench.redwood.ai/acme/2026/shortlist (internal link)
- HF model cards: https://huggingface.co/openplex-7b-ft
- MAP eval template (attached): MAP-eval-template.md

If you want, we can spin up a Dedicated pilot (48-72 hour lead for capacity) with both 7b and 13b nodes and run the A/B automatically. I'll add estimated Dedicated pricing for the 7-day pilot in a follow-up note.

Thanks  happy to workshop the evaluation rubric with your team.

- Dev Patel
